validity.recommendation: Fix CapacityUnits: source says 258 MMSCFD, sheet records 258 MMSCMD (~35x overstatement; CapacityBcm/y=94.17 is physically implausible for a 28-in line). Change to 258 mmscf/d (~2.67 bcm/y).
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's own Capacity [ref] (SCOP technical roadshow PDF hosted on saymar.org, ~2017 vintage per its 1485449570 epoch filename) states verbatim: '258 MMSCFD ultimate capacity of Sales and Fuel Gas 28" pipeline (350 km)' from Rumaila (PS1A) to Al-Najaf (PS3A) — extracted from the PDF text directly (url_verifier cannot token-match inside compressed PDFs; it returns 200 on the bare URL). The sheet copied the number 258 but recorded units as MMSCMD, which cascades to CapacityBcm/y=94.17 and CapacityBOEd=1.5M — a 28-in gas line cannot carry 94 bcm/y (that is ~1.6x TurkStream+NordStream per string). No independent source states any MMSCMD figure. Diameter 28 in and length 350 km ARE confirmed by the same PDF, and length 350 km is independently corroborated by the Jan 2021 Independent Arabia article ('more than 350 km from the North Rumaila fields to Najaf').

validity.recommendation: Disambiguate which physical project this row is: the SCOP EPCF 28-in gas twin (concept/FEED 2017, never built, excluded from the 2024-25 revived crude-only Basra-Haditha project) vs the 2019-approved Basra Oil Company replacement gas line reported near-complete in Jan 2021. Verify whether the latter entered service (possible missing operating pipeline).
validity.researcher_notes: The row conflates two distinct projects. (A) The 28-in / 258 MMSCFD / 350 km specs and the saymar refs belong to the gas component of SCOP's EPCF strategic pipeline (Rumaila PS1A to Al-Najaf PS3A, twin of the 56-in crude line), whose PDF states status 'FEED & EISHA completed for Pump Stations, and Concept for the Pipeline' — i.e., it never reached construction; the project was rebooted in Aug-Dec 2024 as the $4.6bn Basra-Haditha CRUDE pipeline with no gas component mentioned in either the SCOP ministry clarification (gulfoilandgas, 2024-08-06) or AGBI's cabinet-approval coverage (2024-12-31). (B) The ProposalYear/ConstructionYear=2019 and the route narrative trace to the Independent Arabia article (2021-01-19), which describes a DIFFERENT effort: a new gas pipeline approved by the government in 2019, laid along the route of the old decrepit Rumaila-to-Middle-Euphrates gas line under Basra Oil Company projects directorate, 'nearing completion' of pipe-laying in Jan 2021, to feed Samawa and Najaf power plants and cement works. I found NO 2021-2026 EN/AR news of that line's completion, commissioning, or continued construction (searched: Rumaila/Najaf gas pipeline completion; Arabic for the pipeline, Najaf/Samawa power-plant gas arrival, SCOP progress). A corridor gas pipeline project is real (not a phantom), but as recorded — EPCF specs + 2019 construction dates — the specific entity may not exist as such: the EPCF twin never began construction, and the 2019-21 line, if it is the row's subject, may be operating unnoticed. Duplicate check vs the 16-row Iraq gas roster: no other Rumaila/Najaf row; P7573 Basra-Ceyhan and P7459 Faiha-North Rumaila are distinct. Classification (gas, transmission) is correct for either interpretation.

validity.recommendation: Keep Owner = Iraq Ministry of Oil [100%]; do NOT adopt the gem.wiki page's Basrah Gas Company / South Gas-Shell-Mitsubishi attribution.
validity.researcher_notes: Attribution audit: the gem.wiki page (read for leads only) lists operator Basrah Gas Company and owners South Gas Company 51% / Shell 44% / Mitsubishi 5% — that is the shareholding of BGC itself, sourced from Shell's generic BGC corporate page which never names this pipeline (an aggregate-citation existence flag for the wiki claim, not the sheet's). The sheet's own SCOP roadshow PDF states 'MoO will own the assets and operate the pipeline', matching the sheet's Owner1 = Iraq Ministry of Oil 100%. The Jan 2021 article says the gas to be shipped is BGC-supervised production, which makes Rumela a correct FuelSource but does not make BGC the pipeline owner. Endpoints (Rumaila/Basrah -> Al-Najaf) corroborated by both the SCOP PDF (PS1A -> PS3A at Al-Najaf) and the Independent Arabia article.

fills.researcher_notes: Two independent sources agree on 350 km: Independent Arabia 2021-01-19 ('more than 350 km', url_verifier OK with token 350) and the SCOP roadshow PDF ('28" pipeline (350 km)'; PDF verified 200, value confirmed by direct PDF text extraction — verifier cannot token-match compressed PDFs).

Independent Arabia 2021-01-19: the Iraqi government approved the new gas pipeline on this route in 2019 (url_verifier OK with tokens 2019 + Najaf + North Rumaila in Arabic). Single source -> medium. Caveat: 2019 applies to the replacement-line project, not the 2017 SCOP EPCF gas twin whose specs this row carries (see existence concern).
Both sources put the supply at the (North) Rumaila fields: Independent Arabia ('from the North Rumaila fields', Arabic token verified) and the SCOP PDF (start point PS1A at the Rumaila Oil Field).
Endpoints corroborated by two independent sources: SCOP PDF ('From Rumaila (PS1A) to the outlet of (PS3A) at Al-Najaf') and Independent Arabia (North Rumaila fields in Basra to Najaf governorate).

SCOP roadshow PDF: 'MoO will own the assets and operate the pipeline' (value confirmed by direct PDF text extraction; verifier returns bare 200 on PDFs). Single source -> medium. This contradicts the gem.wiki page's BGC/South Gas-Shell-Mitsubishi attribution, which traces to Shell's generic BGC page that never names this pipeline — sheet value is the better-supported one.

No source found that states construction BEGAN in 2019. Independent Arabia (2021-01) shows approval in 2019 and pipe-laying nearly complete by Jan 2021 — consistent with a 2019-2020 start but not explicit — and the SCOP EPCF gas twin (whose specs this row carries) never left FEED/Concept stage. Left unresolved rather than pairing a ref that does not state the number (no orphan/unsupported refs).

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Searched EN + AR (Rumaila/Najaf gas pipeline completion/commissioning; Arabic pipeline name; Najaf/Samawa power-plant gas supply; SCOP progress reports; Iraq Business News; Basra-Haditha reboot coverage). Newest independent evidence: the ministry/SCOP clarification (gulfoilandgas, 2024-08-06) and AGBI's cabinet-approval report (2024-12-31) both describe the revived $4.6bn Rumaila->Haditha project as a CRUDE OIL pipeline only — no accompanying gas line — supporting that the 28-in gas twin this row's specs describe remains not-proceeding, i.e. shelved stands. No news of the 2019-approved replacement gas line (near-complete per Independent Arabia 2021-01) completing or resuming was found in 2021-2026, so no evidence-based upgrade to construction/operating is available either; last positive construction evidence is 2021-01, >2y stale. Shelved was set by GEM 2025-07-14 (<4y), so the 4y->cancelled dormancy rule does not yet apply. CAVEAT (see existence concern): if the 2019-21 Basra Oil Company replacement line was in fact finished, the true status could be operating — but zero independent completion evidence was found, so no change is staged. Confirm shelved.

summary: Real corridor project but the row conflates two schemes (2017 SCOP EPCF 28-in gas twin vs 2019 BOC replacement line, near-complete Jan 2021 then silence); capacity units wrong (source says 258 MMSCFD, sheet has 258 MMSCMD -> 94 bcm/y); shelved confirmed via crude-only 2024 Basra-Haditha reboot coverage; 5 blank refs filled, Construction 2019 unresolved.
